advances: Physical surface-measure transport on actual normal contact in finite compatible families. The theorem concerns conditional ceilings and convex order.
author: PK-research-agent
proof:
First suppose $d\ge2$. For every ordered pair $z,w$ include the body $M_{zw}=(K_z+K_w)/2$. Use the common normal reference $\sigma=\sum_z S_{K_z}+\sum_{z,w}S_{M_{zw}}$, where $S_D$ is the normal marginal of the marked surface measure of $D$. Disintegrate all marked surface laws and the old same-normal tuple against $\sigma$. Write $\mu_{D,u}$ for the finite physical conditional of a body $D$. The original total surface conditional and old tuple conditional have mass at most one, since their normal marginals are dominated by $\sigma$. The endpoint conditionals are dominated by the corresponding original surface conditionals. At almost every normal, each positive body conditional is equivalent to intrinsic Hausdorff measure on its actual support face by the surface disintegration theorem.

Use the conditional ball bound for each triple $(K_z,K_w,M_{zw})$ and for $(K_z,K_w,K_p)$ when $p=(z+w)/2\in P$, the latter only on its tight support set. Each triple's normal reference satisfies $\lambda\ll\sigma$, including when body labels repeat. For $\sigma$-almost every normal with $d\lambda/d\sigma>0$, its three conditional measures relative to $\sigma$ are those relative to $\lambda$ multiplied by $d\lambda/d\sigma$, so the degree-one homogeneous ball inequality transfers. Where $d\lambda/d\sigma=0$ both endpoint conditionals vanish. There are finitely many triples. Thus one common full-measure set suffices for these facts, for face equivalence, and for the old conditional marginals and support conditions.

Fix a normal $u$ in this set and an original parity class of positive conditional tuple mass. The two class submarginals have equal mass because the old midpoint is integer. Every positive cross pair of their input bases has integer midpoint $p\in P$, by lattice completeness. Both surface conditionals for the pair are positive. Apply the ball comparison with $M_{zw}$, for which support contact is automatic, to obtain a positive target conditional. The face-alignment lemma implies that these three actual faces have the same dimension and one direction space. By comparing all cross pairs, all positive input faces of the class have one common dimension $m$ and direction $V$. Their affine hulls have the form $b_z+V$, $b_z\in V^\perp$. In orthogonal physical coordinates use auxiliary bases $(z,b_z)$ and continuous coordinates along $V$. The possible auxiliary output levels are $(p,(b_z+b_w)/2)$, where each product pair lies in $K_p$ by compatibility. Several levels over one $p$ are possible before support contact is imposed.

For $m>0$, take the finite positive intrinsic ball-density representatives on the full-measure good sets of the original endpoint surface laws, set them to zero elsewhere, and use them as endpoint ceilings on the compact actual faces. The alignment lemma for each pair-average triple gives an integrable upper-density representative of $\mu_{M_{zw},u}$ that bounds $H_m(f_z(X),f_w(Y))$ for every product pair from these good sets, where $H_m(s,t)=((s^{-1/m}+t^{-1/m})/2)^{-m}$. All representatives use the same intrinsic Euclidean coordinates on a given level. At a level whose common normal height is below $h_{K_p}(u)$, use the sum of the finitely many pair-average representatives reaching that level as a temporary ceiling. At a level of height $h_{K_p}(u)$, every pair reaching it is tight. The ball comparison gives positivity of the actual target conditional, and the alignment lemma for the tight target triple gives its intrinsic upper-density representative satisfying the same inequality for every producing pair. Its affine hull agrees with the averaged endpoint affine hull. Consequently there is at most one on-support level per physical base $p$, and there use the actual target upper density alone as the ceiling. These are Borel densities of finite integral on the compact possible-output sets. The positive-dimensional variable ceiling theorem applies with weights $1/2,1/2$, finite real auxiliary bases and continuous dimension $m$. Its convex order is the full physical one by the orthogonal coordinate identification.

For $m=0$ the faces are points and the endpoint ceilings are their conditional atom masses. At a tight target level the ball inequality on small balls centered at the two endpoint atoms bounds their minimum by the actual target mass. Face alignment gives the singleton target at their physical midpoint. Use this actual target atom ceiling on each tight level, with at most one such level per $p$. On any other level use the maximum of the finitely many minima of the two atom ceilings of producing pairs. The finite weighted atom theorem then gives the same domination by the chosen ceilings and the same convex order.

In either case apply the finite support roof lemma at $u$. All new midpoint locations are in $C$ with bases in $P$, and the old law is supported on its actual $u$-support graph. Convex order forces the new law onto this graph. On this graph the class law is dominated by $\sum_p\delta_p\otimes\mu_{K_p,u}$, as only the unique on-support auxiliary level over a given $p$ can contribute. This proves pointwise physical feasibility. Moreover only a class having a tight positive product base pair at $p$ can contribute over $p$.

For $d=1$ work at either normal separately with the common normal reference counting the two normals. Every original conditional surface face is an endpoint of unit mass, so the classwise finite atom theorem uses ceiling one at every distinct physical midpoint. The same roof test retains only the actual interval endpoint at each base, so the class law is again dominated by the actual original surface conditional and the same local count applies. This yields pointwise feasibility also in this case.

For assembly apply the Borel density-controlled barycentric kernel theorem to each parity's physical endpoint submarginals, old midpoint kernel and actual target conditional. They have fixed compact supports, bounded masses and Borel versions from disintegration. The pointwise construction proves nonemptiness of the physical coupling constraints, so no measurable choice of auxiliary directions or density representatives is needed. Domination by the actual target gives the support property after assembly. Summing the at most $2^n$ class kernels proves the bound on the marked law. At a fixed $(u,p)$ the local count follows from the necessary tight-pair condition and the classwise bound, and the count is Borel because the bases are finite and the conditional marginal masses are Borel. Integrating the conditional physical convex orders gives the asserted weighted comparisons.

For sharpness use $P=[0,2]^n\cap\mathbb Z^n$ and one fixed convex body $K_z=K$ on each base. Use the entire surface law on bases $\{0,1\}^n$ for the minus marginal and $\{1,2\}^n$ for the plus marginal. Coupling complementary bases and identical boundary points gives an admissible old law. Every integer midpoint forces the plus base to be the coordinatewise complement $2-z$ of the minus base. Thus every admissible output places $2^n$ copies of the surface mass at the single all-ones base, whose reference is one copy. The diagonal boundary pairing attains the bound, also for intervals.
statement:
Let $d\ge1$, $n\ge0$, and let $P=\operatorname{conv}P\cap\mathbb Z^n$ be nonempty and finite. For each $z\in P$ let $K_z$ be a convex body in $\mathbb R^d$. Assume compatibility in the sense that $C=\operatorname{conv}\bigcup_z(\{z\}\times K_z)$ has exact sampled fibers $K_z$. Let $\eta$ be the sum of the ordinary boundary surface measures of $K_z$ on the marked bundle $(u,z,X)$, where $u$ is the almost everywhere unique outward normal (endpoint counting measure for $d=1$). Suppose $\gamma_-,\gamma_+\le\eta$ have an old coupling that preserves the common endpoint normal and whose midpoint $(p,Y)$ has $p\in P$, $Y\in F_{K_p}(u)$ almost everywhere. Then there is one same-normal coupling of the same marginals with the same actual-support midpoint property and $\rho\le2^n\eta$ for its marked midpoint law. Relative to a common finite normal reference, for almost every normal and each original endpoint parity class it has the original two conditional endpoint marginals, and its conditional physical midpoint law dominates the old one in full physical convex order. These orders can be integrated against any bounded nonnegative Borel normal weight.

More locally, its density ceiling over a given $(u,p)$ is the number of classes having positive conditional endpoint bases $z,w$ in that class with $z+w=2p$ and $h_{K_z}(u)+h_{K_w}(u)=2h_{K_p}(u)$. The uniform factor $2^n$ is sharp.
title: Normal-preserving midpoint repair in finite compatible fiber families
